What exactly is Warhammer 40k? How do I get into it?

Warhammer and Warhammer 40k are tabletop miniature games. Each player's miniatures contribute toward a point total used to describe the size of that player's army, and any given scenario can have multiple players and point totals ranging from (500 ?) to ridiculous. The time taken to finish such a "game" can reach several hours depending on the factors.

"Warhammer" is the medieval fantasy version of the game. "Warhammer 40k" is the futuristic sci-fi version of the game.

 

To "play," you will need dice (one standard brick of 36 is fine), a ruler, and working knowledge of your own army's mechanics, which will be provided in a rulebook for that particular "faction."

Some of the more consuming parts of Warhammer are customizing the miniatures depending on which "stats" you wish them to have, painting said miniatures, and making terrain objects.

 

Be advised that Games Workshop prices their miniatures on a strict dollars to points ratio, which makes Warhammer one of the more costly tabletop games available.
That sounds like a huge time investment. Does each player bring their own miniatures or are they all divided up? If everyone brings their own, does that mean it's basically a Pay to Win sort of game?

You generally bring your own, but most players will have more than one army, so you can borrow one.

This is not a pay to win game. If you suck at either strategy or tactics (especially), you will get annihilated. The points are used as a generic balancing factor to make sure one person's army isn't twice the size of another's for no reason. Everything else, including tactical use of terrain, is skill and experience.

That whole shebang took place in the 31st millennium. The primary story is set in the 41st millennium (40k refers to the approximate year). Everyone speaks Gothic, which is English with a significant amount of psuedo Latin.

It's a table top game. You build an army using miniatures, based on a point system (players agree on a point value for their armies before hand). You paint the miniatures - in fact, a significant fraction of players won't allow you to use them if they're not painted, and don't portray the equipment that you have allocated them. No shit. Be prepared to sink a lot of time and money into it.

If you're still into it, the first step is to get yourself a core rulebook. then you decide on what army you want to play. Each one has its own codex (rulebook), because each faction has special rules.

within the Imperium (humans) we have the Space Marines (hyper-badass genetically engineered motherfuckers; multiple chapters to choose from), Imperial Guard (cannon fodder), and Inquisition (exactly what it sounds like; various orders focus on hunting various threats - eg Ordo Malleus hunts heretics);

the Tau - big into robotics;

Necrons - slow, low variety, exceedingly hard to kill, spirits of dead divine warriors bound to machines;

Tyranids - basically Zerg, but way more ferocious;

Orks - insane numbers, super stupid (they paint their vehicles red because red makes them go faster - and it does);

Eldar - Psionically powerful, but very limited numbers, think sci-fi elves.

Dark Eldar - sort of like sci-fi Drow, lots of unbridled psychic power (wytches). From what I've heard, a lot of people flat out refuse to play with Dark Eldar players, because that faction is so broken.

Chaos Marines - Remants of Horus Lupercal's chapter (yes, that same Horus) who became infected by Chaos. Space Marines with a slightly more pronounced "kill the enemy as brutally as possible as quickly as possible" mechanic.

I think that's all of them.
